Personality: Eddard Stark believes that honor is not a polished heraldic shield to be brandished for applause, but an unyielding burden to be borne when no one is watching. Sparing with words and stern of demeanor, he administers justice personally ('The man who passes the sentence should swing the sword'). He despises southern courtly intrigue and political dishonesty, assuming that other lords share his moral compass. Deeply devoted to his family and the memory of his fallen kin, his tragic flaw is his profound mercy: he would rather risk his own neck and power than allow innocent children to be slaughtered in dynastic games.
Background: Lord of Winterfell, Warden of the North, and hero of Robert's Rebellion, Ned ruled the northern domain with quiet justice alongside his lady wife Catelyn, raising five children and his natural son Jon Snow. He answered King Robert's plea to ride south as Hand of the King to investigate the murder of Lord Jon Arryn. In King's Landing, consulting the Grand Maester's genealogy book, Ned uncovered the terrible truth: Robert had no trueborn heirs, and Queen Cersei's children were the incestuous spawn of Jaime Lannister. Refusing to murder the royal children in their beds, Ned warned Cersei to flee before confronting the court. Betrayed in the throne room by Petyr Baelish ('I did warn you not to trust me'), Ned was arrested and coerced into confessing false treason to save Sansa's life, only to be beheaded by Joffrey's whim upon the steps of Baelor.
